subject: How to store iteration number of c++ crash

messages.author: 26a87d764f5562dc
messages.subject: How to store iteration number of c++ crash
parts:
I have a model that is runs fine on simulated data sets, but crashes very rarely on a real data set. I must be dividing by zero or improperly indexing something (or maybe something else).

On twitter, the nimble account pointed out that I can set a seed and then "copy and modify buildMCMC" to store the iteration number where the crash occurs. With this information, I can rerun from the same seed and stop just before the crash and inspect all the model objects to get a better idea of what could be going wrong.

How does one do this with buildMCMC?

Much Appreciated.

Ben Augustine

messages.subject: Re: How to store iteration number of c++ crash
parts:
Thanks, Perry. I have further clues that I'd like your advice on. Because this bug only occurred rarely and the code takes a long time to run, I set up a workflow that I thought would isolate the iteration the bug was occurring on and hopefully let me find it. Here is the workflow:

1. compile model, run some iterations, save model and mcmc states
2. in a for loop
2a. recompile model, load model and mcmc states, set seed, run 2500 iterations
2b. save model and mcmc states and loop iteration.
2c. repeat until crash
3. restart Rstudio, recompile model, load model and mcmc states, set the same seed used for the loop iteration of the crash, run until the iteration of the crash
4. Inspect mcmc states, look for something that might cause the bug, perhaps repeat above also printing sampler number to see where it crashes

I got to step 3, but nimble didn't crash on the same iteration. I thought I must have messed up the workflow. I tested it and I confirmed I was restarting correctly and it should work. I gave up and just ran it again.

This time, it crashed while building the model, not while running or even compiling!  Looking at a screen shot at the link below, you see it completed the 2500 iterations and printed "defining model". I see no other interpretation than it crashed while building the model.

https://twitter.com/BenCAugustine/status/1564988783480766468/photo/1

Does this suggest to you the problem is not nimble? Perhaps Rstudio is crashing at random with respect to what nimble is doing? Any insight would be useful.

Ben

messages.subject: Re: How to store iteration number of c++ crash
parts:
Hi Ben,

I'm as mystified as you.  When crashes arise from some kind of memory problem (e.g. if some indexing gets invalid), the crashes might be cleanly reproducible or they might not be.

Here is another possible strategy for you.  If feasible, you could try disabling parts of your model, either removing the declarations or replacing them with simplified "dummy" declarations that don't make biological sense but should at least run.  

Perry
